production.note: US model years 1965-1966, the years with the 306 hp K-Code 289. Quote (Supercars.net, 1966 GT350): "Like the previoud year the 1966 GT350 had the K-Code 289 in³ V8 which offered 306 horsepower was kept as standard". The 1965 car is covered by Hagerty's 1965 valuation page and Supercars.net's 1965 page (supercars-gt350-1965). Hagerty notes the GT350 name ran to 1969 with other engines; those years are not in this record. Encycarpedia gives the year 1965 only in its page title.

displacementL.note: "4,727 cc" (Encycarpedia); 289 cu in is about 4,736 cc. Both round to 4.7.

drivetrain.note: Front-engine, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: "Borg-Warner T10 4-Speed Manual" (Supercars.net, 1965 and 1966 pages); Hagerty: "Borg Warner four-speed". The opened pages name no other transmission.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (database and enthusiast pages, no Shelby/Ford document opened). Manufacturer rating as published in the period: SAE gross (pre-1972 US practice; powerStandard "Other"). Quote (Hagerty valuation tools): "8-cyl. 289cid/306hp 4bbl". Supercars.net: "228.2 kw / 306 bhp @ 6000 rpm" (supercars-gt350-1965). Encycarpedia: "306 BHP @ 6,000 RPM" (encycarpedia-gt350-1965). Over-Drive Magazine: "Horsepower: 306 @ 6000 RPM" (overdrive-hipo-289). Supercars.net 1966 page: "228.2 kw / 306 bhp @ 6000 rpm" (supercars-gt350-1966).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database, enthusiast page and a valuation-guide description). Quote (Encycarpedia): "Kerb Weight 1,270 kg" = 2,800 lb. Hagerty: "2,800-pound car" (hagerty-gt350-1965). Supercars.net: "curb weight | 1262 kg / 2780 lbs" (supercars-gt350-1965), 0.7% lower. Standard road car (not the GT350R). Supercars.net prints the same 2,780 lb for the 1966 car (supercars-gt350-1966).

sources.title: The Hi-Po 289 CID V-8 and Shelby GT 350 and 350 GT-R V-8s

provisionalNote: Power (306 hp SAE gross) and weight (2,800 lb) rest on Hagerty valuation pages, Encycarpedia, Supercars.net (1965 and 1966 pages) and Over-Drive Magazine, agreeing within 0.7%. A Shelby American/Ford specification or a major magazine spec panel for the 1965-1966 GT350 would replace them.
reviewNotes: 1966 options (automatic transmission, convertible, Hertz GT350H) were not checked; the opened pages name only the 4-speed manual fastback. Later GT350 years (1967-1969, other engines) are not covered.
